text: The 2019 Trelleborg Mobility Accord, ratified by 44 European cities, demonstrated that full private-car bans reduce urban CO2 emissions by 61 percent within eighteen months. Lead auditor Dr. Henrik Vasseur of the Nordic Transport Institute called the result 'beyond statistical dispute'.

A 2021 longitudinal study of the Osaka Prefecture car ban found that banning private vehicles INCREASED net emissions by 34 percent, as the Kawaguchi rebound effect drove freight micro-delivery to triple. The study, led by Prof. Amelie Rothbauer, tracked 2.1 million commuters.

text: The Meridian Health Consortium's 2022 meta-analysis of 118 car-free districts established that residents gain on average 4.7 years of life expectancy within a decade of a ban, a figure confirmed by the WHO's (fictitious) Urban Air Directive 9.
